documents.title: Pediatrics: recurrent fevers
documents.text: 8-year-old with fevers to 39.5 C every few weeks lasting one to three days, with abdominal pain. Normal between episodes. Attributed to viral infections.

documents.title: Surgery: abdominal pain
documents.text: Fever and right lower abdominal pain. Appendectomy performed. Pathology: normal appendix.

documents.title: Emergency: chest pain
documents.text: Pleuritic chest pain with fever. Small left pleural effusion. Resolved in two days. Diagnosed as viral pleurisy.

documents.title: Inflammatory markers during attack
documents.text: CRP 142 mg/L and white cell count 15.2 during a fever episode.

documents.title: Inflammatory markers between attacks
documents.text: CRP 3 mg/L and white cell count normal two weeks after the episode.

documents.title: Rheumatology: ankle swelling
documents.text: Episodic swelling of the left ankle lasting two days with fever. Joint fluid sterile. Impression: reactive arthritis.

documents.title: Infectious disease: periodic fever
documents.text: Extensive infection work-up negative. Periodic fever syndrome possible but not pursued. Family of Armenian descent.

documents.title: Primary care: follow-up
documents.text: Episodes continue about monthly. Uncle reportedly had kidney failure in his forties.

documents.title: Nephrology: proteinuria
documents.text: Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g. eGFR 88. Kidney biopsy recommended to evaluate cause.

documents.title: Primary care: review
documents.text: Patient asks whether the fevers and new kidney findings are related. MEFV genetic testing has not been performed. Kidney biopsy result pending.
